title: Anatomy of an eyeris Object
text: preprocessing .asc EyeLink files eyeris, returned objects class eyeris, contain key components used throughout package’s backend. key components : file: original file path source .asc file block: block number time_orig: raw tracker time (ms) time_secs: normalized tracker time, starting 0 (seconds) eye_x: eye position x-coordinate eye_y: eye position y-coordinate eye: eye (Left Right) recorded data sourced hz: tracker sampling rate (hz) type: whether source data recorded using diameter area method pupil_raw: raw recorded pupil source data arbitrary units (.u.) ’ll notice preprocessing step run, new column added pupil_raw column; new columns follow structure subsequent step appended previous columns name (.e., pupil_raw_{previous steps}_{current_step}). illustrate: pupil_raw -> pupil_raw_deblink -> pupil_raw_deblink_detransient -> … events: list data frames containing trial event messages timestamps blinks: list data frames containing start/stop/durations blinks info: EyeLink EDF header data parsed data frame latest: internal tracker used assessing steps run far confounds: list data frames containing confounding variables preprocessing step (see: 📊 summarize_confounds()) params: detailed list steps run parameters passed step epoch_{name}: list data frames given epoched timeseries Now ’ve explained can expect see running eyeris glassbox() function, ’ll demonstrate glassbox() wrapper generally comprised terms steps defaults implemented.

title: Complete Pupillometry Pipeline Walkthrough
text: (hopefully) shouldn’t encounter , , let us explain: Basically default setting communicating EyeLink machine filtering enabled either live-streamed data saved data EDF files. want filters ’s unclear low-pass filter specifications, conflicts assumption eyeris::detransient() use one-step difference compute threshold detecting large jumps pupil data (suggesting blinking artifacts). general, ’d like data raw possible can “cook” fresh. , data aren’t raw possible, need run eyeris without detransient step. skip detransient step, pass detransient = FALSE glassbox() call. skip detransient step within glassbox pipeline, pass detrend = TRUE glassbox().
code: ***WARNING: SOMETHING OUTRAGEOUS IS HAPPENING WITH YOUR PUPIL DATA!***   The median absolute deviation (MAD) of your pupil speed is 0.  This indicates a potential setup / hardware issue which has likely propogated   into your pupil recording. Most often, this is due to online filtering being   applied directly to your pupil data via the EyeLink Host PC.   WE DO NOT RECOMMEND USING ANY ONLINE AUTO FILTERING DURING YOUR DATA RECORDING.   ***ADDITIONAL INFO*** The default setting for communicating with the EyeLink  machine is to have filtering enabled on either live-streamed data or saved data   in EDF files.  We do not want these filters because:  (1) it is unclear how the EyeLink machine is specifying their low-pass filter,  and (2) it conflicts with an assumption here in `eyeris::detransient()` to use   one-step difference to compute a threshold for detecting large jumps in pupil   data (suggesting blinking or other artifacts).   ***GENERAL TIP***  You should aim to have your data as raw as possible so you can 'cook' it fresh!   ***WHAT TO DO NEXT***  If you would like to continue preprocessing your current pupil data file,  you should consider skipping the `eyeris::detransient()` step of the pipeline   altogether. Advanced users might consider additional testing by manually   passing in different `mad_thresh` override values into `eyeris::detransient()`   and then carefully assessing the consequences of any given override value on   the pupil data; however, this step is not recommended for most users.   PLEASE CONTINUE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

title: Building Your Own Custom Pipeline Extensions
code: winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }

title: Building Your Own Custom Pipeline Extensions
code: #' Winsorize pupil values #' #' Applies winsorization to extreme pupil values within each block. #' #' @param eyeris An `eyeris` object created by [load_asc()]. #' @param lower Lower quantile threshold. Default is 0.01. #' @param upper Upper quantile threshold. Default is 0.99. #' @param call_info A list of call information and parameters. If not provided, #'   it will be generated from the function call. #' #' @return Updated `eyeris` object with new winsorized pupil column. winsorize <- function(eyeris, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99, call_info = NULL) {   # create call_info if not provided   call_info <- if (is.null(call_info)) {     list(       call_stack = match.call(),       parameters = list(lower = lower, upper = upper)     )   } else {     call_info   }   pipeline_handler(     eyeris,     winsorize_pupil,     "winsorize",     lower = lower,     upper = upper,     call_info = call_info   ) }

what: Example C: Epoch with Subtractive Baselining
title: Extracting Data Epochs and Exporting Pupil Data
text: Use 1-second window "DELAY_STOP" baseline apply epoch data. example, ’re extracting 1-second epochs following "PROBE_START" event applying subtractive baseline correction. baseline computed 1-second window corresponding "DELAY_STOP" event. words, means pupil trace normalized subtracting average pupil size pre-probe delay period (.e., baseline period).

title: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing
text: Despite decades pupillometry research, many established packages workflows unfortunately lack design principles based (F)indability ()ccessbility ()nteroperability (R)eusability (FAIR) principles. eyeris, hand follows thoughtful design philosophy results intuitive, modular, performant, extensible pupillometry data preprocessing framework. Much design principles heavily inspired Nipype. eyeris also provides highly opinionated pipeline tonic phasic pupillometry preprocessing (inspired fMRIPrep). opinions product many hours discussions core members signal processing experts Stanford Memory Lab (Shawn Schwartz, Mingjian , Haopei Yang, Alice Xue, Anthony Wagner). eyeris also introduces BIDS-like structure organizing derivative (preprocessed) pupillometry data, well intuitive workflow inspecting preprocessed pupillometry epochs within beautiful, interactive HTML report files (see demonstration ⬇️)! package also includes gaze heatmaps show distribution eye coordinates across entire screen area, helping assess data quality participant attention patterns. heatmaps automatically generated BIDS reports can also created manually.

title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
text: function automatically called glassbox() default. needed, customize parameters detransient providing parameter list. Use glassbox(detransient = FALSE) disable step needed. Users prefer using glassbox() rather invoking function directly unless specific reason customize pipeline manually. Computed properties: pupil_speed: Compute speed pupil approximating derivative x (pupil) respect y (time) using finite differences. Let \(x = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)\) \(y = (y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)\) two numeric vectors \(n \ge 2\); , finite differences computed : $$\delta_i = \frac{x_{+1} - x_i}{y_{+1} - y_i},      \quad = 1, 2, \dots, n-1.$$ produces output vector \(p = (p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n)\) defined : first element: $$p_1 = |\delta_1|,$$ last element: $$p_n = |\delta_{n-1}|,$$ intermediate elements (\(= 2, 3, \dots, n-1\)): $$p_i = \max\{|\delta_{-1}|,\,|\delta_i|\}.$$ median_speed: median computed pupil_speed: $$median\_speed = median(p)$$ mad_val: median absolute deviation (MAD) pupil_speed median: $$mad\_val = median(|p - median\_speed|)$$ mad_thresh: threshold computed median speed MAD, using constant multiplier \(n\) (default value: 16): $$mad\_thresh = median\_speed + (n \times mad\_val)$$

what: eyeris: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing — eyeris-package
title: eyeris: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing — eyeris-package
text: Pupillometry offers non-invasive window mind used extensively psychophysiological readout arousal signals linked cognitive processes like attention, stress, emotional states [Clewett et al. (2020) doi:10.1038/s41467-020-17851-9 ; Kret & Sjak-Shie (2018) doi:10.3758/s13428-018-1075-y ; Strauch (2024) doi:10.1016/j.tins.2024.06.002 ]. Yet, despite decades pupillometry research, many established packages workflows date lack design patterns based Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability (FAIR) principles [see Wilkinson et al. (2016) doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.18 ]. 'eyeris' provides modular, performant, extensible preprocessing framework pupillometry data BIDS-like organization interactive output reports [Esteban et al. (2019) doi:10.1038/s41592-018-0235-4 ; Gorgolewski et al. (2016) doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.44 ]. Development supported, part, Stanford Wu Tsai Human Performance Alliance, Stanford Ric Weiland Graduate Fellowship, Stanford Center Mind, Brain, Computation Technology, NIH National Institute Aging Grants (R01-AG065255, R01-AG079345), NSF GRFP (DGE-2146755), McKnight Brain Research Foundation Clinical Translational Research Scholarship Cognitive Aging Age-Related Memory Loss, American Brain Foundation, American Academy Neurology.

title: Build a generic operation (extension) for the eyeris pipeline — pipeline_handler
code: # first, define your custom data preprocessing function winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }  # second, construct your `pipeline_handler` method wrapper winsorize <- function(eyeris, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99, call_info = NULL) {   # create call_info if not provided   call_info <- if (is.null(call_info)) {     list(       call_stack = match.call(),       parameters = list(lower = lower, upper = upper)     )   } else {     call_info   }    pipeline_handler(     eyeris,     winsorize_pupil,     "winsorize",     lower = lower,     upper = upper,     call_info = call_info   ) }  # and voilà, you can now connect your custom extension # directly into your custom `eyeris` pipeline definition! custom_eye <- system.file("extdata", "memory.asc", package = "eyeris") |>   eyeris::load_asc(block = "auto") |>   eyeris::deblink(extend = 50) |>   winsorize()  plot(custom_eye, seed = 1) #> !
